limits: These are selected paraphrased public facts, not copied full source pages or a rebase API authorization promise.

facts: GITHUB_TOKEN is a GitHub App installation access token limited to the workflow repository.
The job receives a short-lived token; this changes authentication class from the earlier OAuth credential, not the endpoint contract.
Workflow/job permissions modify token defaults; unspecified permissions become none.
A same-repository push avoids the fork pull-request downgrade. Some higher policy can restrict writes; requested YAML is not a measured effective capability.
Published stack read/create endpoints support installation tokens with pull-request read/write respectively.
The inspected page does not document the discovered whole-stack rebase route, so those grants do not establish rebase requirements.
The supported built-in token can authenticate requests without registering a new app.
A different app/token can require additional setup; no app registration or secret addition is proposed here.
